# GitHub-Native AI Documentation Ecosystem — Knowledge Base

> Structured distillation of a six-platform documentation research corpus and the resulting
> AI-augmented docs-as-code architecture. 31 topic pages + glossary, Markdown with YAML frontmatter
> carrying id, tags, sources, confidence and related-page links. Start at INDEX.md.

- [Localization Models for Docs Platforms — Five Patterns and the EN-Canonical Strategy](00-foundations/i18n-models.md): The six-platform field exhibits every localization architecture that exists in practice: filesystem locale copies (Docusaurus, Mintlify), plugin-assembled multi
- [Markdown, MDX, and Frontmatter — Content Formats as Contracts](00-foundations/markdown-mdx-frontmatter.md): "Markdown" is not one thing: the six platforms span CommonMark-adjacent MDX v3, the Python-Markdown/pymdownx dialect, Hyperbook's `:::` directive extension, and
- [Mermaid and Diagrams-as-Code — Rendering Models, Validation, Syntax Discipline](00-foundations/mermaid-diagrams-as-code.md): Diagrams-as-code stores diagrams as text (Mermaid) in the same Git repository as prose, making them diffable, PR-reviewable, AI-editable, and CI-validatable. Al
- [Search Models for Docs Sites — Local Build-Time Index vs. SaaS vs. Black Box](00-foundations/search-models.md): Documentation search comes in three architectures: a build-time local index executed client-side (lunr, flexsearch, Zensical's Disco), an external SaaS index qu

- [Hyperbook — Profile (76.0/100; The Wildcard — Great Mechanism, Wrong Audience, Bus Factor 1)](10-platforms/hyperbook.md): Hyperbook is an MIT-licensed TypeScript/Node SSG built for interactive educational workbooks (OER), maintained essentially by one person (Mike Barkmin, OpenPatc

## Architecture Patterns
- [AI in CI, Never in Serving](20-patterns/ai-in-ci-not-in-serving.md): All AI output is produced at build/CI time (or via a local CLI), committed through pull requests, and only then served as static files. The published site has z
- [Canonical vs Generated Content — Structural Separation](20-patterns/canonical-vs-generated-separation.md): AI-derived documentation must never silently become authoritative. This pattern makes the boundary between human-owned canonical knowledge and AI-generated deri
- [Hash-Based Drift Detection and Incremental Regeneration](20-patterns/hash-based-drift-detection.md): Every generated page records a sha256 content hash of each source document it was derived from. CI recomputes those hashes at HEAD; any mismatch flags the page 
- [Leveled Retrieval — Deterministic First, Escalate on Evidence](20-patterns/leveled-retrieval.md): Context for AI generation is assembled by four escalating levels: L1 deterministic file selection (adopted), L2 build-time full-text index, L3 embeddings, L4 hy
- [Metadata & Provenance as a Frontmatter Contract](20-patterns/metadata-provenance-contract.md): Every page's YAML frontmatter is a schema-validated contract, not decoration. Canonical pages declare identity, audience, the repo paths they document, and owne
- [PR-Gated Generation — Bot Branch, Run Report, Human Approval](20-patterns/pr-gated-generation.md): AI output persists exclusively through pull requests: the bot commits to `docs-gen/*` branches, the PR carries a machine-produced run report, branch protection 
- [Task Contracts — Bounded Generation Instead of Free-Form Prompting](20-patterns/task-contracts.md): Every AI generation job references a named, versioned YAML contract that defines what the task may read, what it must produce, which deterministic gates its out
- [Thin Provider Abstraction — Protocol, Four Adapters, YAML Routing](20-patterns/thin-provider-abstraction.md): Model access sits behind one Python Protocol (`complete(task_meta, messages, opts) → {text, usage, provider, model}`), four ~40-line HTTP adapters (Anthropic, G

## Best Practices
- [Bilingual Documentation (EN/HU) — Canonical Language plus Fallback](30-best-practices/bilingual-docs-en-hu.md): Bilingual capability without bilingual fork drift: English is the single canonical authoring language; Hungarian lives as filesystem-mirrored copies under `i18n
- [CI Quality Gates — The Deterministic Gate Ladder](30-best-practices/ci-quality-gates.md): Every PR (human or bot) passes an ordered ladder of deterministic, merge-blocking checks: lint → frontmatter schema → internal links → Mermaid compile → full bu
- [Evidence Discipline — Tagged Claims and Calibrated Honesty](30-best-practices/evidence-discipline.md): Every factual capability claim in the research corpus carries an explicit evidence tag, invention of unverifiable facts is banned by a named list, and proprieta
- [GitHub Actions Security for AI Pipelines](30-best-practices/github-actions-security.md): When CI holds AI provider keys and write access, the workflows themselves become the primary attack surface. The distilled posture: least-privilege permissions 
- [Prompt Injection Defenses for Generation Pipelines](30-best-practices/prompt-injection-defenses.md): A pipeline that feeds repository content (including user-submitted questions and its own previous output) into LLMs must assume injection attempts are present.

- [Build vs Buy vs Host — SaaS and OSS-Static Decision Logic](40-decision-frameworks/build-vs-buy-vs-host.md): The six-platform field split cleanly into hosted SaaS (Mintlify, GitBook) and OSS static generators (Docusaurus, MkDocs, Zensical, Hyperbook), and the decision 
- [Maintenance Risk Assessment — Judging Repo Health and Successor Dynamics](40-decision-frameworks/maintenance-risk-assessment.md): An OSS dependency's biggest risk is rarely its code; it is whether anyone will be maintaining it in two years. The corpus assessed this with a structured repo-h
